question: Which indigenously developed missile was successfully test fired by DRDO and Indian Navy on 26 March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertically Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vertically Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VL-SRSAM)** was successfully test-fired by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and the **Indian Navy** on **26 March 2025**.
 
• VL-SRSAM is a **state-of-the-art indigenous missile system** designed to counter aerial threats such as fighter aircraft, drones, and helicopters at close ranges.
 
• The missile is equipped with **advanced radar systems** and a **radio frequency seeker** for precise target detection and tracking.
 
• The successful test was conducted from an **Indian Naval Ship off the coast**, demonstrating its capability to neutralize aerial targets in a vertically launched mode.
 
• This missile plays a crucial role in enhancing the **self-reliance** of India in defense technology, aligning with the **‘Make in India’ initiative**.
 
• The VL-SRSAM has a range of approximately **40 km**, making it suitable for defending naval vessels from aerial threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Short-Range Sea-to-Surface (Coast) Missile:**

 
 
• This type of missile is designed for targeting enemy installations or vessels near the coast.
 
• It generally has a smaller range compared to medium or long-range missiles.
 
• Currently, India does not have a specific missile categorized under this name.
 
 
 
• **Advanced Short Range Air-to-Air Missile:**
 
 
• These missiles are primarily designed for air-to-air combat between fighter aircraft.
 
• They are equipped with infrared or radar seekers for precise targeting.
 
• One example is the **ASRAAM**, developed by MBDA, but it is not indigenously developed by India.
 
 
 
• **Short-Range Anti-Tank Missile:**
 
 
• This category includes missiles designed to penetrate armored vehicles and tanks.
 
• India has developed the **Nag missile**, which falls under this category but is not relevant to the current test conducted on 26 March 2025.
 
 
 
• **Vertically Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile:**
 
 
• The VL-SRSAM is indigenously developed by DRDO for the **Indian Navy**.
 
• It is designed to provide quick reaction defense capabilities against aerial threats.
 
• This missile is launched vertically and can engage targets at a range of up to **40 km**.
 
• Its features include **advanced electronic warfare systems**, precise targeting capabilities, and high mobility.
 
• It is a part of India’s efforts to strengthen its defense technology and reduce dependency on foreign imports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO’s Role:**

 
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** is responsible for the development of advanced defense technologies in India.
 
• DRDO has been instrumental in achieving self-reliance in missile technology through projects like **Agni, Prithvi, and Akash**.
 
• The VL-SRSAM is a testament to India’s capability to develop cutting-edge defense systems indigenously.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy’s Preparedness:**
 
 
• The successful test-firing of VL-SRSAM showcases the Indian Navy’s preparedness to counter aerial threats.
 
• Integration of such advanced missile systems into naval vessels significantly enhances maritime security.
 
• It also demonstrates the collaboration between DRDO and the Indian Navy in strengthening defense capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• The VL-SRSAM aligns with the government’s **‘Make in India’ initiative**, aimed at promoting indigenous manufacturing and reducing dependency on foreign imports.
 
• Such developments are crucial for achieving self-reliance in critical sectors like defense.
